title: Adsorption Behavior of Methylene Blue, Cd2+, and Pb2+ Onto Raw Bamboo Shoot Brown Powder: Kinetic, Isotherm, Thermodynamic, and Regeneration Studies
content:
Raw bamboo shoot brown powder (BSBP) was developed as a low-cost biosorbent for removing methylene blue, Cd2+, and Pb2+ from wastewater. Its porous structure enabled efficient adsorption through surface interactions, achieving high removal efficiencies under optimized conditions. BSBP also exhibited good regeneration and reusability, providing an eco-friendly, sustainable, and cost-effective approach for wastewater treatment.


ABSTRACT

Textile wastewater containing synthetic dyes and toxic heavy metals poses a serious environmental concern. This study investigated raw bamboo shoot brown powder (BSBP) as a low-cost biosorbent for the removal of methylene blue (MB), Cd2+, and Pb2+ from aqueous solution. Batch adsorption experiments were performed by varying pH (2–9), adsorbent dosage (0.25–6.0 g), contact time (5–240 min), initial concentration (10–200 mg L−1), and temperature (25°C–35°C). Maximum removal efficiencies of 98% for MB, 85% for Cd2+, and 80% for Pb2+ were achieved at pH 6 using 2.0 g of adsorbent. Equilibrium was attained within 180 min for MB and 120 min for Cd2+ and Pb2+. The adsorption kinetics were best described by the pseudo-second-order model, while isotherm analysis indicated heterogeneous adsorption behavior. FTIR and SEM analyses supported the role of functional groups and porous morphology in adsorption. Overall, findings suggest BSBP is a sustainable and promising adsorbent for wastewater treatment.
